Petitioner is before this Court in this petition filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C. seeking anticipatory bail in Cr.No.24/2023 registered against him at Sadshivanagar police station for offences punishable under Sections 466, 120B, 418, 406, 419, 420, 465, 469, 471, 474, 417, 463 and 464 IPC.
2. The aforementioned crime was registered based on a private complaint filed by one Sujay Ammath, which was referred to police for investigation.

3. Brief facts of the case are that the complainant is the absolute owner of certain properties situated at Achaiah Chetty layout, Mekhri Circle, Bangalore, by virtue of a settlement deed executed by her grandfather in the year 1980.

She is running a Hospital from 1985 and she NC: 2023:KHC:21656 wished to start a Multi Speciality Hospital in the adjacent property which was leased from one Mr.A.C.Srinivas Raju of Subhadra Srinivas Raju Trust.

Loan was raised to the tune of Rs.7.25 Crores on 02.11.2012 from the Karnataka State Financial Corporation (for short 'KSFC') on the security of the schedule property and the hospital commenced operations in 2013 in the name 'Diagram Healthcare Pvt. Ltd'.

However, due to unforeseen circumstances, the liability on the hospital started to raise and the loan repayments to KSFC which were regular till 2015 started to default and there was an outstanding loan to the tune of Rs.9.00 Crores in the year 2015 for which the KSFC started recovery process by issuing demand and recovery notices and the hospital functioning also came to a standstill.

At this juncture, the accused/petitioner became acquainted with the complainant in 2018 and expressed his intention to give financial assistance and to revive the hospital and also undertook to clear the outstanding loan of KSFC, subject to the condition that the schedule property was sold to him.

Therefore, an NC: 2023:KHC:21656 agreement of sale drafted by the accused came to be registered in his favour for a consideration of Rs.13 Crores, less than the actual market value prevailing then in June 2018.
The accused also insisted for blank cheques as security.
A registered supplementary agreement got executed on 24.09.2018.

4. The allegations are that out of the sale consideration only Rs. 9.00 Crores was paid under the Sri. Subramanya Konanur vs State Of Karnataka on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48343728/

documents, shown to be towards the repayment of the KSFC loan, without a single pie paid to or utilized by the complainant.
Further, after the agreements were got registered, the accused did not discharge the outstanding loans of KSFC, which led to issuance of sale notices by the KSFC.
Further, the accused has tampered and misused the blank cheques issued in his favour as a security and presented them for encashment without intimating the complainant.

Further, the accused filed a suit for a specific performance before the City Civil Court in O.S.No.1129/2021 seeking to enforce the agreement of NC: 2023:KHC:21656 sale dated 13.06.2018 and consequently withdrew the said suit, stating in the memo that an absolute sale deed has been executed and registered in his name in respect of the schedule property.

5. According to the complainant, the absolute sale deed dated 26.08.2021 has come into existence during the subsistence of the charge of KSFC under fraudulent circumstances and after passing of orders of winding up of the Company namely Diagram Healthcare Pvt. Ltd. of the complainant in Company Petition No.213/2015.
Further, the said sale deed has been executed with the aid of the General Power of Attorney dated 13.06.2018 by committing fraud.

It is contended that the General Power of Attorney alleged to have been executed by the complainant and her husband in favour of the petitioner is not at a genuine document and thus, it is contended that there is a prima facie case against the petitioner for the offences now registered against him.
NC: 2023:KHC:21656 6.
As per the petitioner, the agreement of sale executed between the petitioner and the complainant is a registered document, as per which the sale consideration was fixed at Rs.12 Crores.
Out of which, Rs.4,00,75,000/- was shown to be paid.
The balance was supposed to be paid at the time of registration.

Further, an advance sale consideration of Rs.50 lakhs was paid against Rs.4,00,75,000/- as shown in the agreement and on the same day General Power of Attorney was executed by the complainant and her husband in favour of the petitioner.

It is also contended that the General power of attorney was not registered and consequently the same has been adjudicated upon an application made by the petitioner and the duty and penalty was paid on 16.08.2021.
It is further contended by the learned Senior Counsel that since charge was created over the property in favour of KSFC, NOC for sale of schedule property was issued by them to the complainant.
Thereafter, supplementary sale agreement was executed between the petitioner and the complainant in the office of Sub-Registrar, Gandhinagar, NC: 2023:KHC:21656 Bangalore.

Since sale consideration was increased to Rs.13 Crores and further charge over the property was not cleared by the complainant and under the supplementary agreement, another sum of Rs.8,00,50,000/- was paid with an understanding that the charge created in favour of KSFC would be cleared by the petitioner.
7.
The petitioner has submitted the details of payment to the KSFC to the tune of Rs.9.00 Crores through the account of the complainant as per the terms of the agreement.
It is submitted that the balance payable to the complainant is in fact payable to the KSFC by the petitioner.

It is also brought to the notice of the Court that since the documents pertaining to the property was in possession of KSFC, the petitioner has preferred Crl.P.No.7294/2020 seeking direction to KSFC to accept the balance amount towards the closure of the loan and issue of NOC and the said criminal petition is Sri. sentences.text: It is contended by the learned Senior counsel for petitioner, transaction between the petitioner and the complainant is purely civil in nature.
The complainant is trying to give the flavour of criminal offence, in order to coerce the petitioner to agree for unreasonable demands of the complainant.
The allegations that the GPA has been forged etc., cannot be gone into in this petition.
Admittedly, there was a suit for specific performance which was withdrawn on the basis of registration of a sale deed.
The criminal petition is pending consideration wherein the petitioner has sought for closure of the loan amount and to issue direction to the KSFC.
It is also not in dispute that, major part of the amount has been paid.
The allegations have to be proved in due course.
Petitioner has undertaken to co-operate with the investigation of the case.
9. In view of the above facts and circumstances, the petitioner has made out sufficient grounds to grant NC: 2023:KHC:21656 relief as sought for in this petition.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER i. Petition is allowed.
ii. Petitioner/accused is directed to be released in the event of his arrest in Cr.No.24/2023 of Sadashivanagar Police, subject to the following conditions:
(a) Petitioner/accused shall appear before the Investigation Officer within a period of one week from the date of receipt of a copy of the order and in that event he shall be released on his executing a bond in a sum of Rs.2,00,000/-
[Rupees two lakhs only] with two sureties for the likesum.
(b) He shall furnish proof of his  residential address and furnish  the contact number and shall  inform the I.O/Court, if there is  any change in the address or  contact number.
(c) He shall not leave the jurisdiction  of the trial Court without prior  permission of the learned trial  Judge, till conclusion of the  investigation.
